`markup` must be a string; otherwise raise `TypeError`. Find `button` elements with a `data-action` attribute. For each, collapse all whitespace in its visible text—including text inside nested elements—to single spaces and strip its ends. Strip the attribute value as well. Ignore a button when either result is empty. Attribute order and case must not matter, and character/entity references must be decoded.

Return a dictionary mapping normalized button text to its action. Preserve first-insertion key order, but if later markup repeats the same normalized text, replace that key's value with the later action. Gracefully accept incomplete markup: finalize an unclosed button at end of input, ignore unmatched closing tags, and when a new button begins inside an unclosed button, finalize the earlier one first. Return `{}` for empty input.

import unittest from solution import collect_button_actions class CollectButtonActionsTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_nested_visible_text_attributes_entities_and_case(self): markup = ''' ''' self.assertEqual( collect_button_actions(markup), {'Save & Close': 'save&close', 'Go Next': 'next'}, ) def test_ignores_missing_or_empty_values(self): markup = ( '' '' '' '
Not a button
' ) self.assertEqual(collect_button_actions(markup), {}) def test_duplicate_text_replaces_value_without_reordering(self): markup = ( '' '' '' ) result = collect_button_actions(markup) self.assertEqual(list(result.items()), [('Same', 'two'), ('Other', 'middle')]) def test_incomplete_nested_button_finalization(self): markup = ( '' '' first = collect_button_actions(markup) second = collect_button_actions(markup) self.assertEqual(first, second) self.assertIsNot(first, second) if __name__ == '__main__': unittest.main()
